title: G.S. Garments Ltd.
pitch: A multilingual garment-manufacturer website with product, fabric and content administration.
highlights: Session authentication, CSRF protection and first-party analytics
imageKind: Local application captures · fictional demo data
audience: buyers exploring garment collections and staff maintaining the catalogue
overview: A manufacturer needs a website that can explain its collections to visitors and remain manageable for the people maintaining it. G.S. Garments Ltd. connects a multilingual public catalogue with an authenticated workspace for products, events, fabrics and traffic reports.
engineering: The application uses server-rendered PHP with explicit routing, controllers and repositories. PDO handles relational queries and search pagination, while session authentication and CSRF checks protect administration. First-party traffic aggregation gives the management interface its own reporting workflow.
details: Public pages are language-prefixed with JSON translation dictionaries for 12 languages, plus theme controls and responsive templates.
Searchable, paginated product and event catalogues, image galleries, fabric content and a downloadable company profile.
A versioned MySQL schema, first-party traffic aggregation with CSV export, contact-form validation and throttling.
Plain PHP 8.1+ with a small front controller and router; no Composer or Node build step is required.

title: MediKart BD
pitch: A pharmacy commerce platform with a SvelteKit storefront and Express API.
highlights: Product catalogue, customer accounts and storefront flows
Inventory, store, order and prescription API routes
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: MediKart BD brings a pharmacy storefront and its API together as one commerce platform. Customer browsing, account routes and product discovery connect to staff administration and point-of-sale screens, with backend records for inventory, stores, orders and prescriptions.
engineering: SvelteKit provides the customer and staff interfaces, while Express and Mongoose organise API operations and MongoDB records. Redis supports caching alongside mail-service boundaries. The frontend/backend split gives the business workflow a dedicated interface layer and a separate data and service layer.

title: NextSet
pitch: A workout companion that keeps going when the connection doesn’t.
highlights: Workout templates, weekday plans and repeating sequences
Weekly analysis and deterministic domain logic
imageKind: Cover composition based on existing Android screenshots
audience: people planning routines and tracking workouts offline
overview: NextSet is built around the part of a workout that happens away from a desk: choosing a plan, completing sets and returning to a session without losing its structure. It supports fixed weekdays and repeating sequences, alongside a weekly view of planned and completed work.
engineering: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose provide the native interface, while Room stores plans and workout history locally. Immutable session snapshots and transactional checkpoints preserve execution state. Scheduling and progress calculations live in deterministic domain logic, supported by 41 unit tests.
details: Fully offline: no account, ads, analytics or cloud services, on Android 7.0 and above.
Supersets with unequal set counts, and rest overrides for individual sets, including the last set and zero rest.
Holding for one second completes a set; the rest countdown turns red and waits for acknowledgment, with pause, skip and undo available.
Optional adaptive or manual reminders, light, dark and large-text support, and workout duration estimates from configured rests and time per set.

title: Safoyana Digital Print
pitch: From a print specification to an organised order queue.
highlights: Configurable print products and quantity-based pricing
Customer orders and a staff management workspace
JWT roles, ownership checks and server-calculated totals
audience: print-shop customers specifying an order, and staff organising the order queue
overview: Print orders involve more than adding a product to a basket: the paper stock, quantity and specification all matter. This application brings those choices into one customer flow and gives staff a structured workspace for reviewing the resulting orders.
engineering: The Next.js storefront communicates with a modular NestJS API. Prisma models users, products and order items in PostgreSQL; the API calculates quantity-based totals and enforces authenticated roles and record ownership. Validated DTOs and relational modelling keep the ordering workflow structured across the customer and staff interfaces.
details: Customers choose stock, quantity and artwork; uploaded artwork is attached to the order configuration.
Totals are calculated on the server from stored quantity price tiers instead of trusting submitted values.
Updating order items runs in a Prisma transaction, and customers can change or cancel only pending orders.
Built with Next.js 16, React 19 and Zustand on the front and NestJS 11 with Prisma 7 behind it. There is no payment gateway or shipping integration.

title: TalenTrack
pitch: Recruitment records meet searchable candidate documents.
highlights: Separate web, API and model services
audience: teams exploring data, research and local automation
overview: TalenTrack brings job openings, applicants and candidate documents into a recruitment workspace. Its scope extends from application forms and applicant records to PDF ingestion and local-model-assisted retrieval, making it a useful example of several services supporting one workflow.
engineering: A React frontend connects to Express/PostgreSQL for recruitment records. A separate FastAPI service handles document ingestion with pgvector embeddings and local Ollama models, keeping conventional record management and model-backed retrieval in distinct service boundaries.
details: Candidates browse open jobs and apply with a PDF resume; recruiters log in to manage postings and applicants.
Uploaded resumes are parsed, embedded and stored in PostgreSQL with pgvector, so recruiters can ask the AI chatbox questions across all candidates.
Inference runs locally through Ollama (all-minilm embeddings, llama3.2:1b), and Docker Compose starts every service together.
A seeding script generates realistic jobs and 15 detailed sample resumes for testing.

title: DermaCare
pitch: A cosmetics commerce platform combining storefront, store administration and API.
highlights: Cosmetics catalogue, cart and wishlist interfaces
Express/MongoDB commerce API with authentication and caching
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: DermaCare combines the cosmetics storefront and its commerce API into one project. Product discovery, cart and wishlist interactions sit alongside store-administration screens, connecting customer-facing shopping flows with the records and operations behind the shop.
engineering: A SvelteKit frontend consumes an Express API backed by MongoDB. Authentication middleware, product and commerce routes, Redis caching and mail-service boundaries organise the backend, while reusable frontend components present catalogue, cart, wishlist and administration workflows.

title: Clipping
pitch: A photo-services order workspace, from image submission to order summaries.
highlights: Consistent frontend structure across the dashboard
audience: photo-services
overview: Clipping brings image submission, service selection, order summaries and account views into a consistent photo-services dashboard. Its step-by-step interface turns a detailed order brief into a more approachable customer journey.
engineering: The dashboard organises a photo-service order into distinct steps: submitting images, choosing services and reviewing the summary. Consistent form layouts and account views give customers a clear path through a detailed task, while staff-facing layouts keep order information easy to scan.

title: Lovebird Association of Bangladesh
pitch: A club’s public website and editorial administration workspace, presented as one project.
highlights: Public articles, events and member pages
Separate public and editorial applications with shared API integration
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: LAB combines a public club website and its content-management workspace in one project. Visitors explore articles, events and members, while the administration interface supports the editorial work behind that content. Related article-layout work provides a focused reading experience for longer-form stories.
engineering: Two SvelteKit applications serve distinct public and editorial workflows through shared API integrations. The public frontend presents managed records as browseable content, while the admin panel provides article, event and member-management interfaces. The separation keeps content presentation and editing responsibilities clear.

title: PATH Smoking Resumption Prediction
pitch: Making longitudinal research understandable, one outlook at a time.
highlights: Separate population models for smoking transitions
Local JSON-model inference and contribution explanations
audience: researchers exploring smoking transitions, uncertainty and model behaviour
overview: Reclaim turns a longitudinal smoking-transition study into an explorable research interface. A fixed-choice questionnaire routes a fictional profile to the relevant population model, then presents cumulative outlooks, uncertainty and contributing factors together with the evidence needed to interpret them.
engineering: A fingerprinted plain-JSON survival-model bundle supports local inference. Separate former-, current- and never-established-smoker populations, interval-censored outcomes and grouped explanation contributions make the modelling decisions visible alongside uncertainty and research evidence.

title: Notepad AI
pitch: A focused writing space, with room for a local AI assistant.
highlights: Persistent note library with a focused writing interface
Local completions and streamed assistant chat through Ollama
audience: individual writers managing a local note library with optional local-model assistance
overview: Notepad AI brings a persistent note library, a focused editor and local AI assistance into one writing workspace. Writers can move between notes, develop ideas with an assistant, and keep their content saved as they work.
engineering: A Next.js frontend connects to a FastAPI backend with SQLite persistence. Debounced saving keeps editing fluid, while Ollama powers local completion and streamed chat workflows. The Ollama integration was tested during development, bringing note management and local-model assistance together without requiring a hosted AI provider.
details: Notes are created, renamed, edited and deleted through a FastAPI API backed by SQLite, with debounced autosave after about 1.2 seconds.
Inline completions are accepted with Tab, and a chat panel can use the open document as context.
Model selection, downloads and streaming all go through a local Ollama instance, with adjustable debounce, output length and context size.
Designed as a single-user local tool: there is no authentication or per-user isolation.

title: Hood Up
pitch: Workshop booking and vehicle service workflows on Android.
highlights: Local queue and cache with advisor fallback
audience: people using software on Android devices
overview: Hood Up explores vehicle-service booking from an Android application. Workshop discovery and booking sit alongside local queue/cache handling, bringing customer-facing interactions and connectivity concerns into the same mobile project.
engineering: Java activities integrate Firebase and Firestore, with repository security rules forming part of the data-access boundary. The local queue and cache provide additional implementation depth beyond a collection of static Android screens.
details: Customers browse workshops, add cars, book services and track appointments; admins manage services and workshops from a dashboard.
Cloud Firestore holds online data while SQLite provides local storage and offline caching.
An Ask chatbot gives service suggestions through the Gemini API, with local fallback suggestions when no key is available.
Android services, background threads, broadcasts and notifications support appointment reminders.

title: Car Shop Management System
pitch: A Java desktop showroom connecting vehicle inventory, customer purchases and tested business logic.
highlights: Separate customer showroom and inventory administration
Vehicle-specific pricing tools and customer purchase logs
31 passing JUnit tests across domain logic and purchase workflows
imageKind: Local Swing application captures · fictional demo data
audience: customers exploring vehicles and staff managing a car-shop inventory
overview: Car Shop Management System brings a small dealership workflow into a Java desktop application. Customers create a local profile, browse commuter and sports cars, explore cost estimates and purchase a vehicle. An administration view connects vehicle entry with inventory statistics and customer purchase records.
engineering: Swing panels and a CardLayout organise the customer and administration views around separate inventory, vehicle and customer classes. A shared vehicle abstraction supports commuter and sports-specific calculations. The JUnit 5 suite exercises pricing, search boundaries, customer summaries and the purchase workflow across multiple domain classes.
details: Originally developed for CSE110 object-oriented programming and extended for CSE430 software testing.
Commuter vehicles expose insurance and trip-cost estimates; sports cars add maintenance and quarter-mile calculations.
Purchasing removes the selected vehicle from inventory and updates customer spending, VIP status and the administration log.
Profiles and inventory are held in memory for the current session. The administration switch is a demonstration interface, without authentication or a database.

title: Microservice Ecommerce
pitch: An exploration of event-driven commerce service boundaries.
highlights: Separate user, catalogue, cart and order services
audience: engineering teams interested in backend and service design
overview: Microservice Ecommerce explores a shopping system divided into user, catalogue, cart, order and notification services. Its focus is the coordination of distinct business responsibilities and the data each service owns.
engineering: RabbitMQ connects parts of the service architecture, with Prisma, MongoDB and Redis used across different persistence concerns. The repository provides concrete material for discussing message-based coordination, independent data models and service boundaries.
details: Five services with their own stores: users, products (MongoDB with Elasticsearch search), cart (Redis), orders (PostgreSQL via Prisma) and notifications.
Placing an order publishes a RabbitMQ message that the notification service turns into a confirmation email.
JWT with user and admin roles, bcrypt password hashing, Joi validation, rate limiting and Helmet; PM2 and concurrently manage the services.

title: P2P File Stream
pitch: Explore files moving directly across the local network.
audience: engineering teams interested in backend and service design
overview: P2P File Stream connects local-network discovery, connection handshakes and file delivery in one workflow. Each stage has a clear responsibility, making it a useful example of how peers find each other and coordinate a transfer.
engineering: Bonjour provides local discovery, Socket.IO coordinates peer handshakes, and Node.js streams the transfer. The React frontend presents the connection flow while the receiving side writes files to the native Downloads location.
details: Devices on the same Wi-Fi are discovered automatically through mDNS (Bonjour), with no configuration.
Files stream directly between devices over Axios, with no intermediate server storage.
Socket.io drives live progress bars for large transfers, and received files are saved to the Downloads folder.

title: Secure Note Taking
pitch: Private notes with a community and administration layer.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Secure Note Taking combines private note management with community and administration views. It explores the difference between personal content and shared application data, with authenticated routes and role-aware interfaces supporting those separate uses.
engineering: The React client connects to Express controllers and MongoDB records. JWT middleware, roles and explicit ownership checks protect private-note access on the server, where the security boundary belongs.
details: One login serves users and admins; the app decodes the JWT to show the matching view.
Users keep private notes with full CRUD, fully separated from other accounts, and can read and post in a public community feed.
Admins manage users, moderate content and see database statistics from MongoDB aggregations, such as grouping users by shared interests.
The whole stack runs in Docker Compose, with Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.

title: BDJobs Scraper
pitch: Turn job listings into structured, salary-normalised records.
audience: teams exploring data, research and local automation
overview: The job-data collector explores turning browser-rendered listings into structured reports. Salary normalisation is part of the processing step, so extracted values can be compared more consistently than raw page text.
engineering: Puppeteer and its cluster tooling coordinate browser extraction in Node.js. The script separates collection and record normalisation from saving report output, while remaining dependent on the structure and availability of the external source site.
details: Collects company, title, URL, salary and mentioned technologies from BDJobs IT listings.
Classifies each job by primary stack (Node.js, Java, PHP, .NET or Python) and records when other stacks are mentioned.
Groups salaries into predefined buckets per stack and writes both a JSON dataset and a readable text report.
Stealth plugin, clustered workers, random delays and periodic checkpoints keep long runs steady. It is a personal project built to answer the author's own questions.

title: Regro Media
pitch: A service-led website for a marketplace and brand-management agency.
highlights: Clear positioning for marketplace and brand-management services
Strategy sections, case-study media and enquiry calls to action
audience: businesses needing a clear public web presence
overview: Regro Media introduces a marketplace-management agency through a service-led landing page. The page connects a clear opening message with strategy information, client presentation, case-study media and enquiry calls to action, giving prospective customers a structured way to explore the offer.
engineering: SvelteKit and reusable Svelte components organise the navigation, hero, service strategy, client, case-study and footer sections. Tailwind utilities keep layout and styling consistent across the page, while the section structure supports a clear visitor journey from introduction to enquiry.

title: Instagram Clone
pitch: A social application exploring feeds and real-time conversations.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Instagram Clone is an earlier social-application project spanning posts, conversations and notifications. Its archival gallery provides a broader view of the interface, while the source shows how several related social features share user records and real-time events.
engineering: A Svelte frontend communicates with Express and Sequelize/PostgreSQL persistence. Socket.IO listeners support the message and notification side of the application, separate from the ordinary request/response routes.

title: Group Chat
pitch: A compact real-time conversation app with named rooms.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Group Chat explores real-time conversation through named rooms, users and messages. The interface keeps the scope small enough to focus on room-based interactions instead of the wider social features found in the Instagram Clone project.
engineering: Express serves the application while Socket.IO coordinates room and message events. MongoDB provides a persistent message model alongside the real-time transport, separating stored records from transient connections.

title: FileShare API
pitch: Authenticated uploads and link-based file sharing.
audience: engineering teams interested in backend and service design
overview: FileShare organises authenticated uploads and shareable links behind a focused API. Upload handling, file records and sharing routes provide a clear example of turning a file-management workflow into backend responsibilities.
engineering: Express routes use JWT authentication, upload handling and share-link controllers. Prisma/PostgreSQL and Redis dependencies support persistence and caching boundaries around the file workflow.
details: Accounts must confirm their email before uploading files.
Each file can be shared through a unique, time-limited link backed by a signed token.
Redis caches file paths; Joi validates input, Helmet sets secure headers and a rate limiter guards against spam.

title: Photo Editor Backend
pitch: An exploration of service boundaries for image workflows.
audience: engineering teams interested in backend and service design
overview: This project explores backend service boundaries for image workflows. Gateway, access, image and notification services organise distinct responsibilities, with image-processing and observability configuration providing a concrete view into the architecture.
engineering: Express services use RabbitMQ and Redis alongside Sharp image processing. The gateway provides a single entry point, while service-specific routes separate access, processing and notification concerns. Container and observability configuration makes the infrastructure relationships easier to inspect.
details: Real-time collaborative editing: several users work on an image at once over socket.io, with a JWT checked on every WebSocket message.
User service (PostgreSQL, Prisma), image service (MongoDB, Multer, Sharp) and notification service (Redis, Nodemailer) communicate through RabbitMQ.
Docker Compose runs the full stack behind an Nginx reverse proxy and an API gateway, monitored with Prometheus and Grafana.
Known limitation: WebSocket connections work only directly against the image service, not through Nginx or the gateway.

title: FinShark Backend
pitch: An API exercise in stocks, comments and portfolio data.
audience: engineering teams interested in backend and service design
overview: FinShark organises stock, comment and user-portfolio data behind an authenticated API. Its typed endpoints and explicit persistence structure make it a clear example of backend application organisation.
engineering: ASP.NET Identity and JWT authentication sit alongside Entity Framework and repository abstractions. The stock, comment and portfolio areas show how request handling, identity and persistence can be organised into separate responsibilities.
details: A .NET 9 Web API structured with controllers, services, repositories, DTOs and interfaces.
Separate account, stock, comment and portfolio controllers, with ASP.NET Core Identity issuing JWTs.
Entity Framework Core persistence and auto-generated Swagger documentation.

title: BD Walks API
pitch: Structured region and walking-route data behind a typed API.
audience: engineering teams interested in backend and service design
overview: BD Walks models regions and walking routes behind a structured API. Region, walk and image endpoints connect location-oriented records with typed request handling and role-based access.
engineering: ASP.NET Core supplies the typed HTTP layer, Entity Framework handles persistence, and DTO mappings separate transport shapes from stored entities. Role policies add an explicit authorisation layer to protected operations.
details: A .NET 9 API for managing walking tracks and regions in Bangladesh, including image upload to local storage.
JWT authentication with Reader and Writer roles over CRUD for regions, walks and images.
AutoMapper DTO mapping, action-filter validation, central exception-handling middleware, Serilog logging and Swagger documentation.

title: Medicine Data Scraper with Proxy Rotation
pitch: A browser automation pipeline for structured product data.
audience: teams exploring data, research and local automation
overview: This automation utility collects structured medicine-product information and can send updates to a product API. It combines browser extraction and network configuration in a pipeline intended to move data between systems.
engineering: Node.js and Puppeteer handle browser-driven collection, with rotating proxy support and Axios requests for the update boundary. That makes live execution operationally different from reading a static dataset.
details: Collects generic name, strength, brand and price for tablets and capsules from medex.com.bd.
Each session rotates its proxy, viewport and user agent, scrolls like a person and restarts automatically after failures.
Scraped records are pushed to a backend API, which also needs a working proxy list to avoid Cloudflare blocking.

title: eAppair
pitch: An app landing page built around a distinctive visual identity.
audience: businesses needing a clear public web presence
overview: eAppair introduces an app concept through a distinctive landing page, using product illustrations and particle effects to establish its visual character. The sections lead visitors through the offer with a clear, consistent presentation.
engineering: Product illustrations and motion give the landing page a recognisable identity, while the section structure helps visitors follow the offer. Consistent styling connects the app concept, its features and the visual story across the page.

title: Kyra
pitch: A finance-themed landing page with a bold visual language.
audience: businesses needing a clear public web presence
overview: Kyra is a finance-themed marketing frontend with a strong visual identity. Its archival screenshots show the landing-page composition, supporting sections and longer page presentation as a piece of web-design implementation.
engineering: Illustrations, supporting sections and a distinctive visual identity work together to explain a complex offer. The page pairs a confident introduction with a consistent visual hierarchy, making the service story easier to follow.

title: Studio Website
pitch: A website design for a studio client, from homepage to full-page layout.
highlights: Homepage and full-page layout designed for a client brief
Clear visual hierarchy across a long-form page
audience: studio visitors learning what the studio does and how to get in touch
overview: A studio needs a website that presents its work and services clearly to visitors. This client project covers the design of the homepage and the complete page layout, shared as a case study on Dribbble.
engineering: This project is a design deliverable rather than a coded application. The work focuses on layout, typography and visual hierarchy, with the homepage and a full-page view showing how sections flow from introduction through to the closing call to action.

title: Plaidea
pitch: A digital agency website with a confident visual identity.
audience: digital-agency services
overview: Plaidea presents a digital agency through a service-led marketing website. Its visual hierarchy gives the offering and supporting work a consistent structure across the page.
engineering: The page gives the agency a consistent visual presence across its introduction, work and service sections. Strong imagery and a clear reading order help visitors understand what is offered and where to go next, without relying on unsupported client statistics or testimonials.

title: Landify
pitch: A technology-focused landing page built for clear product storytelling.
audience: technology storytelling
overview: Landify is a technology-focused landing page arranged around product storytelling. Its sections give the page a progression from an introduction to more detailed supporting content.
engineering: The page introduces the product idea, breaks down its offer into supporting sections and carries the visual identity through the full layout. It demonstrates how a technology business can present an unfamiliar service through clear hierarchy, consistent illustration and concise information blocks.

title: Bizzency
pitch: A business landing page balancing service information and visual character.
audience: business-service presentation
overview: Bizzency is a business landing page built around an introduction, service information and supporting sections. It demonstrates balancing a strong visual treatment with content a visitor can scan.
engineering: The page balances a memorable opening with sections that explain the business and its services. Consistent spacing, visual hierarchy and supporting imagery help visitors move from an introduction toward more specific information about the offer.

title: Beatls
pitch: A creative agency frontend focused on work and services.
audience: creative-agency presentation
overview: Beatls is a compact creative-agency frontend focused on introducing work and services. Its page composition is the main deliverable, giving the business concept a consistent visual presence.
engineering: The site introduces the creative agency through a sequence of work, people and service sections. The emphasis is on a coherent visual language and a clear browsing experience that lets the work support the agency’s message.

title: Estern
pitch: A mobile-solutions business website with a clear service structure.
audience: mobile-solutions services
overview: Estern presents a mobile-solutions business through a service-led website. A strong introduction, supporting sections and consistent visual styling help visitors understand the company’s focus and explore its offer.
engineering: The page translates a mobile-solutions offer into an accessible business presentation. A strong opening, service sections and consistent visual styling give visitors a way to understand the company’s focus without needing detailed technical knowledge.

title: Portability
pitch: A service-led website for discovering local care.
audience: local-care discovery
overview: Portability presents a local-care service through an information-led frontend. The work centres on making the service proposition and next steps visible within a multi-section landing-page structure.
engineering: The page leads with the care-service offer, then uses supporting sections to explain the options and build a clearer picture of the service. The full-page view shows the overall story, while individual views let visitors inspect the information hierarchy and visual consistency.

title: Staylowkey
pitch: A healthcare discovery frontend with clear information hierarchy.
audience: healthcare discovery
overview: Staylowkey presents healthcare discovery through service listings, specialist information and profile-related interfaces. Clear content hierarchy helps visitors understand the offer and find their next step.
engineering: The design connects service discovery with provider information, registration and profile-related layouts. Consistent forms and a clear section hierarchy bring a complex service into a coherent, approachable browsing experience.

title: Kerstfeest
pitch: A seasonal campaign page with a festive visual direction.
audience: a seasonal campaign
overview: Kerstfeest is a Christmas-themed campaign frontend. It uses seasonal visuals and a section-based landing-page structure to give a short-lived promotional idea a cohesive web presentation.
engineering: A seasonal visual direction connects the introduction and promotional sections into one campaign page. The work shows how a short-lived offer can still have a complete, considered presentation, with a consistent style from the opening section to the end of the page.

title: Valentina
pitch: A themed campaign page for Valentine’s Day.
audience: a themed campaign
overview: Valentina is a Valentine’s Day-themed frontend, built as a cohesive promotional page. Visual character and section composition are the focus of this earlier website work.
engineering: The seasonal theme runs through the imagery and section composition, giving the campaign a consistent character. The page carries the visual direction from its opening section through the supporting content, creating a complete promotional presentation.

title: Map Veto
pitch: A small, purpose-built map selection tool for competitive play.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Map Veto focuses on a single competitive-play task: narrowing a pool of maps through selection and veto interactions. Its small scope keeps attention on the decision, with map imagery providing an immediate visual reference.
engineering: The experience keeps attention on a single decision: which maps remain in play. Clear map imagery and separate selection/results views make the interaction understandable without a larger tournament interface getting in the way.

title: Sketchbox
pitch: A playful canvas for drawing and experimenting with colour.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Sketchbox is a small interactive drawing tool built around a canvas and colour palette. It is a focused example of direct manipulation in the browser, with the visual interaction itself carrying most of the product value.
engineering: Svelte and JavaScript coordinate drawing and palette state around the browser Canvas API. The compact interface keeps attention on colour and direct interaction, creating a focused space for visual experimentation.

title: Soundboard
pitch: A small audio library for uploading and playing sounds.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Soundboard is a small audio-library application for uploading and playing sounds. User controllers and a separate API extend the scope beyond a static collection of audio buttons, while the archival images document the earlier interface work.
engineering: A Next.js frontend connects to Express and MongoDB. The upload and playback flow spans the browser interface and backend records, giving the application a clear media-management boundary.

title: Studio Ghibli Movies
pitch: A compact way to browse films and explore their details.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Studio Ghibli Movies is a small film-browsing frontend with list and detail views. It explores presenting external API content as an approachable browsing experience, with shared state connecting the collection and individual film pages.
engineering: Svelte components and a shared frontend store organise film information around an external API. Collection and detail views keep browsing connected while presenting each film’s content in a consistent visual structure.

title: CSE302 — Canteen Management
pitch: Coursework connecting canteen records with staff reports.
audience: people managing day-to-day business or personal workflows
overview: Canteen Manager is coursework connecting canteen records with staff-oriented reporting. It demonstrates a practical relational CRUD application, bringing a browser interface, request handlers and SQL fixtures into the same project.
engineering: A React frontend talks to an Express backend with MySQL persistence. The included schema/fixtures and reporting routes provide concrete examples of how an academic business workflow maps into relational records.

title: Monkeytype Automator
pitch: A small browser automation experiment.
audience: teams exploring data, research and local automation
overview: A compact browser-automation experiment exploring how a script can drive a typing interaction. The project focuses on browser control and repeatable actions, providing a small, inspectable example of task automation.
engineering: Node.js and Puppeteer coordinate the browser session and typing actions. The concise script keeps the control flow easy to inspect and provides a focused example of programmatic interaction with a web interface.
